label: sequence began with d: original-phase steps 3+ and <DEL>
explanation: Fires when the first original token is d (93% of activation mass; rate 33.5% vs about 1% for other first tokens). It fires from step 3 of the original phase through the <DEL> step, with the strongest activations at t=4-5 and decay toward <DEL>. Top examples all begin d d. Weaker, low-magnitude firing also happens when d is the second original token. It essentially never fires at t<=2 or in the copy phase (0.1% of mass), even though d is output there. Whatever the input token at the current step is has little effect. At the <DEL> step of L=9 sequences it is often inactive. Dev split: P=0.95, R=0.69, F1=0.80, mass recall=0.93; the misses are mostly bottom-quartile activations.

issues: Test F1 is 0.798, which is below 0.8. The claim that it 'rounds to the bar' is generous. Mass recall (0.928) and precision (0.955) are real, but they hide a systematic gap: 31% of active steps are missed (32,772 on test). Bottom-quartile coverage is 0.12 and second-quartile coverage is 0.62.

Systematic miss class: sequences where d is the SECOND original token. The test misses list is full of them (3 d c o..., s d s z..., y d n..., 0 d l e...). On dev, (orig(1)==d)&(orig(0)!=d)&t>=3&phase<=1 has precision 0.28 and covers 19.6% of active steps, against 10.5% for sequences with no d in the first two positions.

The explanation calls the d-second firing 'weak' and treats it as one block (adding it gives P 0.62). That misses the structure: firing depends heavily on the first token. With orig(1)==d, the rate is about 0.47-0.56 when orig(0) is in {a,c,f,s,u,i,w,y,0,v,m,b}, and about 0 when orig(0) is in {e,g,j,n,o,z,1,t}. So the d-second case is not uniform noise.

Claims that check out: zero firing at t<=1 and almost none at t=2 (0.0% mass). Copy phase is 0.1% of mass. Mass peaks at t=4 (31.6%). For first-d sequences, firing at <DEL> is rare when L=9 (precision 0.25) and nearly certain when L<=6 (0.999). first_tok=d holds 93% of mass with a 33.5% rate. Cutting at t<=7 gives precision 0.997, so the false positives are late steps in long sequences.
There is some low-magnitude firing in sequences without d in the first two positions, boosted when prev_tok is in {j,g,z,n} (rate 4.4%). It is 0.9% of mass, so this is noise.
